Oxidative stress has been linked to fibromyalgia pathophysiology, with antioxidant therapies proposed to reduce elevated lipid peroxidation and mitophagy.
Melatonin was shown to improve brain function in a Gulf War Syndrome model through modulation of oxidative stress.
Fibrinolysis-resistant micro-clots described in the vasculature of Long COVID patients may trap inflammatory molecules and impair oxygen exchange, linking oxidative stress to chronic illness.
Micro-clots and platelet hyperactivation, potentially driven by elevated oxidative stress, may also play a role in ME/CFS pathology, similar to findings in Long COVID.
Muscle biopsies from ME/CFS patients have revealed cellular membrane damage likely attributable to elevated reactive oxygen species levels.
Comorbid fibromyalgia and ME/CFS results in increased illness severity and greater symptom burden compared to either condition alone.
Inflammatory biomarker differences have been observed based on PEM severity in ME/CFS, suggesting distinct underlying physiological mechanisms by severity level.

Plasma amino acid profiles of athletes after exercise (decreased leucine, isoleucine, asparagine, methionine, lysine, glutamine, alanine, and certain lipids) resemble baseline metabolic profiles of ME/CFS patients, suggesting impaired exercise-response capacity.
The RECOVER study reported that ME/CFS diagnoses have increased significantly since the COVID-19 pandemic, with many Long COVID patients now meeting ME/CFS diagnostic criteria.
Malato et al. (2023) estimated that over 1,000 participants per group would be required in ME/CFS studies to adequately account for diagnostic misclassification, a scale beyond most current studies.

About half of the nearly two million people with Long COVID in the UK now meet clinical criteria for ME, with some shared biomedical and physiological features, though it remains unclear if the conditions are identical.
UK prevalence of ME is estimated at 250,000 to 400,000 people.
The economic cost of ME to the UK in 2014/15 was estimated at £3.3 billion per year.

Analysis of Hospital Episode Statistics for the 'postviral fatigue syndrome' code (ICD-10 G93.3) showed a 50-fold difference in diagnostic rates between white females over 41 and non-white males aged 0-40.
Diagnostic rates for the 'postviral fatigue syndrome' code were one-fifth as high in non-white males and females compared with corresponding white groups at all ages.
GPs practising in the most deprived areas of England were least likely to record a diagnosis of ME.

In the DecodeME study, only 3.3% of participants self-reported an ethnicity other than White, compared with 18.3% of the England and Wales population identifying as 'nonwhite' in the 2021 census, indicating under-representation of minoritised groups in ME research.
Diagnosis of ME is typically delayed by several years from symptom onset, contributing to under-diagnosis particularly in under-served groups.
A series of Manchester papers (2013-2014) found barriers at every stage of diagnosis and management of CFS/ME for people from Black and minority ethnic groups.

UK public funders (MRC and NIHR) provided £8.05 million in ME grants over 10 years, equating to £2.88 per person with ME compared with £74 per person per year of overall public health research funding, illustrating gross underfunding relative to disease burden.

A case series of five people with very severe ME requiring tube feeding revealed serious care defects, including allowing severe malnutrition, inappropriate psychological diagnoses, and long delays before starting enteral feeding.

The authors call for trials of repurposed drugs already used extensively elsewhere, including low-dose naltrexone and treatments for mast cell activation syndrome and orthostatic hypotension, as promising but unproven ME therapies.

Historical aetiological hypotheses attributing ME to deconditioning or psychosomatic causes, and denial of patients' illness experience, are described as having caused years of epistemic injustice and continuing to underlie poor healthcare decisions.
Stigma is described as a contributory factor in poor healthcare experiences and induces trauma in people with ME.

Published ME research, including studies using UK Biobank data, has often omitted participant ethnicity even when available, and little published research specifically includes people from minority communities.
Several published surveys of GPs and other healthcare workers have found low levels of knowledge and widespread misconceptions about ME.

Regression analysis of sociodemographic factors on G93.3 diagnostic status, controlling for medical factors, indicated that individuals who are socially deprived are less likely to have received a G93.3 diagnosis, suggesting register-based sampling underrepresents this group.

The study introduces an online respondent-driven sampling method combined with validated DePaul University CCC algorithms as a novel approach to reduce selection bias when estimating characteristics of a Canadian Consensus Criteria (CCC) myalgic encephalomyelitis population, compared to relying on ICD G93.3 register data alone.
Women with preeclampsia had significantly higher depression, anxiety, and chronic fatigue syndrome scores than healthy pregnant women.
Serum soluble CTLA-4 (sCTLA-4) levels were significantly higher in preeclamptic women than in healthy pregnant controls.
Serum soluble CD80 (sCD80) levels were significantly higher in preeclamptic women than in healthy pregnant controls.
Serum copper levels were significantly higher in preeclamptic women compared with healthy pregnant controls.
A composite z-score index (z sCTLA-4 + z sCD80) was significantly increased in preeclamptic women compared with controls.
Serum albumin was significantly lower in preeclamptic women compared with healthy pregnant controls.
Serum magnesium was significantly lower in preeclamptic women compared with healthy pregnant controls.
Serum calcium was significantly lower in preeclamptic women compared with healthy pregnant controls.
Serum vitamin D was significantly lower in preeclamptic women compared with healthy pregnant controls.
Serum zinc was significantly lower in preeclamptic women compared with healthy pregnant controls.
The sCTLA-4/sCD80 ratio was significantly lower in preeclamptic women compared with healthy pregnant controls, suggesting a shift toward heightened immune activation.
Serum GM-CSF levels did not significantly differ between preeclamptic women and healthy pregnant controls.
In a regression model including blood pressure, systolic and diastolic blood pressure and sCD80 (positively) and magnesium (inversely) explained 68.2% of variance in the Fibro-Fatigue (CFS) score.
Blood pressure, sCD80 and copper (positively), and albumin (inversely) explained 62.4% of variance in the HAMA anxiety score.
Systolic/diastolic blood pressure, sCD80, and sCTLA-4 explained 59.4% of variance in the HAMD depression score.
Excluding blood pressure, sCTLA-4, sCD80, and BMI (positively) plus vitamin D, calcium, and GM-CSF (negatively) explained 58.0% of variance in the HAMD depression score.
Excluding blood pressure, sCD80, sCTLA-4, and copper (positively) plus albumin and vitamin D (negatively) explained 56.2% of variance in the HAMA anxiety score.
Excluding blood pressure, sCTLA-4, copper, and sCD80 (positively) plus vitamin D, calcium, and magnesium (inversely) explained 55.8% of variance in the Fibro-Fatigue (CFS) score.
The z sCTLA-4 + z sCD80 composite score was positively and significantly correlated with Fibro-Fatigue, HAMA, and HAMD scores.
The sCTLA-4/sCD80 ratio was inversely and significantly correlated with Fibro-Fatigue, HAMA, and HAMD scores.
sCTLA-4, copper, and having a child (positively) plus calcium and vitamin D (inversely) explained 71.6% of variance in systolic blood pressure.
sCTLA-4 and copper (positively) plus vitamin D, calcium, and GM-CSF (negatively) explained 48.0% of variance in diastolic blood pressure.
In the fully adjusted model, pre-existing chronic fatigue syndrome (CFS) or fibromyalgia was associated with significantly higher odds of more severe first SARS-CoV-2 infection symptoms.
Pre-existing chronic lung condition was independently associated with higher odds of more severe first SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Pre-existing high blood pressure was independently associated with higher odds of more severe first SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Pre-existing weakened immune system status was independently associated with higher odds of more severe first SARS-CoV-2 infection.
Pre-existing arthritis was independently associated with higher odds of more severe first SARS-CoV-2 infection in the primary (confirmed or suspected infection) model.

Pre-existing osteoporosis was independently associated with lower odds of a more severe first SARS-CoV-2 infection, a likely artifact of excluding COVID-19 deaths (which are more common in osteoporosis patients with fractures).

When the analysis was restricted to confirmed SARS-CoV-2 infections, arthritis was no longer significantly associated with severity, whereas pre-existing mental health condition became significantly associated with more severe infection.
Reporting pre-existing fatigue or loss of appetite (as chronic health symptoms) was associated with higher odds of more severe first SARS-CoV-2 infection in the main model.

When chronic conditions were recoded by duration prior to infection, only high blood pressure and CFS (or fibromyalgia) remained significantly associated with more severe infection among conditions diagnosed less than 10 years before infection.

In the sensitivity analysis using a binary (severe/hospitalized vs. not) severity outcome, CFS or fibromyalgia remained significantly associated with more severe infection, while chronic kidney disease newly emerged as significantly protective.

A significant sex-by-bowel-disorder interaction was observed: females with a bowel disorder diagnosed 10 or more years before infection had higher odds of more severe infection than females without bowel disorders, while no such association was seen in males.

Sex significantly interacted with BMI in predicting infection severity: in males, higher BMI/excess body weight was associated with higher odds of more severe infection, whereas no such association was found in females.

The authors propose that because fibromyalgia is triggered by mental stress and anxiety, the indirect psychological impact of the COVID-19 pandemic may have exacerbated fibromyalgia symptoms coincidentally with an actual SARS-CoV-2 infection, potentially explaining the observed association.

The authors cite a Swedish study reporting that SARS-CoV-2 infection can potently trigger reactivation of latent herpesviruses and endogenous retroviruses in individuals with pre-existing chronic fatigue syndrome.

Patients with HSD/hEDS-associated chronic pain showed significant reductions in pain severity across multiple domains on the SF-MPQ-2 and BPI from baseline through all follow-up intervals up to 18 months.
Pain-VAS scores decreased significantly from baseline at 1, 6, 12, and 18 months following CBMP prescription.

Health-related quality of life, measured by the EQ-5D-5L index, increased significantly from baseline at all follow-up intervals, with improvements seen in mobility, usual activities, pain/discomfort, and anxiety/depression subscales.
Self-reported sleep quality (SQS) improved significantly from baseline at all follow-up timepoints, with further improvement seen between early timepoints and 18 months.
GAD-7 anxiety scores decreased significantly from baseline at all subsequent follow-up periods.
Patient Global Impression of Change (PGIC) scores showed further individual improvement between 1 month and 6, 12, and 18 months.
By 18 months, 18.01% of patients achieved a clinically significant (MCID) improvement in BPI pain severity, 25.47% in BPI pain interference, and 25.47% on the Pain-VAS.
In univariable logistic regression, a CBD dosage greater than 25 mg/day was associated with increased odds of achieving a clinically significant improvement in BPI pain severity at 18 months.
In multivariable logistic regression, CBD dosage >25 mg/day was no longer significantly associated with a clinically significant improvement in pain severity.

On multivariable logistic regression, being a former cannabis user (versus cannabis naive) was associated with increased odds of reporting a clinically significant improvement in pain severity at 18 months.
Being a current cannabis user at baseline was not significantly associated with a change in the odds of reporting a clinically significant improvement in pain severity.

Adverse events were reported by 31.06% of patients (50/161), with a total of 601 adverse events documented (373.29% cumulative incidence), most commonly of moderate severity, and no life-threatening or disabling events occurred.
The most commonly reported adverse events among patients with HSD/hEDS prescribed CBMPs were headache, fatigue, lethargy, nausea, and somnolence.
Genetic sequencing identified a heterozygous COL1A1 c.572G>A (p.Gly191Asp) mutation, a characteristic glycine substitution, consistent with a rare OI/EDS overlap collagen type I disorder.
The patient developed severe aortic regurgitation with non-coronary cusp retraction and a severely dilated left ventricle, attributed to collagen-related valvular compromise in the OI/EDS overlap.
Histopathology of the excised aortic valve showed non-specific degenerative changes with mucin deposits in the valvular stroma, consistent with connective tissue disease-related valve degeneration.
A cited study reported perioperative mortality exceeding 20% in patients with collagen-related disorders undergoing cardiac surgery, mainly due to bleeding complications.

Bioprosthetic aortic valve replacement (rather than mechanical valve) was chosen for this high-bleeding-risk patient, consistent with prior literature indicating bioprosthetic valves yield better outcomes than mechanical valves in osteogenesis imperfecta patients.

A preoperatively planned preventive sternal cerclage with surgical steel wires was used and proved effective in preventing sternal dehiscence at 12-month follow-up in this patient with fragile sternal bone.
Cardiac-valvular EDS patients frequently develop mitral valve disease (usually prolapse), while aortic valve compromise, though less common, is also reported.
Physical examination showed a phenotype combining OI and EDS features: high palate, elevated nasal bridge, low-set ears, blue sclerae, finger and knee joint hypermobility, and hyper-elastic skin.

At 12-month postoperative follow-up the patient remained asymptomatic with a normofunctional bioprosthetic valve and normal left ventricular function, indicating a favorable surgical outcome despite the underlying connective tissue fragility.
Kyphoscoliotic (type 6) Ehlers-Danlos syndrome is caused by mutations in the PLOD1 gene, which encodes lysyl hydroxylase 1 (LH1), leading to LH deficiency.
As an alternative genetic cause, kyphoscoliotic EDS (type 6) can also result from mutations in FKBP14, which encodes the FK506 22 kDa binding protein.
Patients with EDS type 6 characteristically present with blue sclera, corneal ectasia, and ocular fragility due to lysyl hydroxylase deficiency.

In a cited case series of 11 patients with EDS type 6, all patients showed corneal thinning and substantial risk of corneal swelling and rupture, with 7 of 11 having experienced corneal rupture spontaneously or after minimal trauma and one with a history of corneal hydrops.

A 7-year-old girl with known EDS type 6 developed sudden diminution of vision, pain, redness, and photophobia in her right eye following trivial trauma from a fingernail, later diagnosed as a Descemet's membrane tear with acute corneal hydrops.

Intracameral injection of isoexpansile 20% sulfur hexafluoride (SF6) gas to tamponade the Descemet's membrane tear failed, as the tear extended to the limbus and the gas escaped into the intracorneal space.
Attempted placement of a central compression suture on the fragile cornea led to full-thickness spontaneous corneal rupture intraoperatively, illustrating the risk of suturing brittle EDS corneas.

Cyanoacrylate tissue adhesive glue was successfully used to seal the intraoperative full-thickness corneal rupture as a chemical bandage, followed by intracameral air tamponade, leading to progressive anatomical and visual improvement over 6 months.
The patient's left eye showed diffuse limbus-to-limbus corneal thinning with topography suggestive of keratoglobus and diffuse corneal ectasia, distinct from the acute right eye hydrops.

Paterson's 1993 review of 39 infants with multiple unexplained fractures in contested child abuse cases identified parental joint hypermobility as one of several risk factors associated with infant bone fragility.

In Holick et al's 2017 study of 72 contested child abuse cases with infant multiple unexplained fractures, 93% of infants had clinical evidence of h-EDS and/or a family history with a parent confirmed to have h-EDS.
In the same Holick et al cohort, vitamin D deficiency (25OH-Vitamin D <20 ng/mL) was found in 66% of tested infants and 53% of tested mothers, often co-occurring with h-EDS.

In Miller et al's 2019 case series of 75 infants with multiple unexplained fractures in contested child abuse cases, h-EDS was identified as a risk factor in 20% of infants, far exceeding the estimated 0.2% general population prevalence.

The author proposes that h-EDS increases infant fracture risk primarily via a biomechanical mechanism: fetal joint hypermobility (and a potentially softer maternal uterus in h-EDS mothers) reduces fetal bone loading during pregnancy, weakening fetal bone, rather than via an intrinsic bone structural abnormality.
The author notes that h-EDS is an autosomal dominant connective tissue disorder for which no causative gene has yet been identified, unlike other Ehlers-Danlos syndrome subtypes.
The author states that young infants born to mothers or fathers with h-EDS or joint hypermobility are at increased risk of fragility fractures, based on multiple prior reports.

A nearly 10-year-old Catahoula Leopard dog with dermatosparaxis-type Ehlers-Danlos syndrome carried a previously published homozygous missense variant in ADAMTS2 and displayed a milder clinical phenotype than typical dEDS cases.
Light microscopy of the affected dog's skin showed markedly reduced density of collagen fibers that were randomly oriented and appeared shorter than normal.

Electron microscopy showed variable fibril diameters and scattered irregular cross-sectional profiles, but the collagen fibrils lacked the characteristic 'hieroglyphic' appearance seen in dogs with a frameshift ADAMTS2 variant, suggesting a milder ultrastructural phenotype.
The authors conclude that dogs with dEDS, like other species, can show variable disease severity including a spectrum of dermal collagen abnormalities depending on the underlying ADAMTS2 variant.
Miscarriage occurred in 23 of 121 pregnancies (19.0%) in women with vascular EDS, roughly double the general Dutch population miscarriage rate.
Miscarriages were significantly more common in women carrying a glycine substitution in COL3A1 compared to women with other variant types.
Stillbirth occurred in 3 of 121 pregnancies (2.5%), attributed to placental infarction, placental abruption, and one of unknown cause.
Preterm birth occurred in 18 of 94 completed pregnancies (19.1%) among women with vascular EDS.
Spontaneous preterm birth was more than doubled in women with vascular EDS compared to singleton pregnancies in the general Dutch population.
Preterm prelabour rupture of membranes (PPROM) occurred at a higher rate in women with vascular EDS compared with the general Dutch population.
Severe perineal tears (third/fourth-degree) occurred almost 10 times more often in women with vascular EDS having vaginal delivery than in the general Dutch population.
Postpartum haemorrhage occurred about three times more often in women with vascular EDS than in the general population.

No uterine ruptures, arterial dissections, vascular complications, or pregnancy-related deaths occurred in this cohort, in contrast to prior literature reporting mortality rates of 4.9%-6.6% and multiple uterine rupture cases.
The specific type of COL3A1 variant was not significantly correlated with occurrence of postpartum haemorrhage or severe perineal tears.
There was no significant correlation between COL3A1 variant type and frequency of spontaneous preterm birth.
Women with a COL3A1 haploinsufficient variant appeared less likely to experience pregnancy-related complications than those with dominant-negative (e.g., glycine substitution) variants.

The authors' cohort data support performing elective caesarean section before 37 weeks gestation in women with vascular EDS to reduce risk of uterine rupture, severe perineal tears, and cardiovascular stress from labour, while balancing neonatal respiratory distress syndrome risk.
Among women with a preconception vEDS diagnosis, most (6/9, 66.7%) underwent an elective caesarean section because of their vEDS diagnosis, generally without complication.
Only a small minority of women with vEDS (16.3%) recalled being informed about reproductive options such as pre-implantation genetic testing and prenatal diagnosis, highlighting a counseling gap.
Congenital anomalies were detected prenatally in three children of vEDS-affected mothers, including cleft lip/palate, single umbilical artery, and clubfoot.
Three neonates born to vEDS mothers suffered intracranial bleeding during vaginal delivery, one with lasting multiple disabilities.

The authors hypothesise that reduced functional collagen type III in the decidua and placental villi impairs trophoblast invasion and immune tolerance establishment, potentially explaining the high miscarriage rate observed in vEDS pregnancies.
Vascular EDS, caused by COL3A1 mutations, was rare among aortopathies but showed a very strong association with spontaneous arterial rupture events.
Patients with vascular EDS undergoing surgery had significantly higher postoperative complication rates than other aortopathy patients.
Vascular EDS is estimated to affect between 1 in 50,000 and 1 in 200,000 individuals, and may be underreported due to misdiagnosis.
COL3A1 mutations cause defective or reduced synthesis of type III collagen, weakening vessel walls and predisposing them to dilation and rupture.
Vascular EDS presents with translucent skin, easy bruising, distinctive facial features, and complications including recurrent pneumothorax, intestinal rupture, and uterine rupture during pregnancy.
Diagnosis of vascular EDS relies on clinical criteria, family history, and molecular genetic testing for COL3A1 pathogenic variants.
A clinical trial found that celiprolol, a vasodilatory beta-blocker, significantly reduced the rate of arterial dissections and ruptures in vEDS patients compared to untreated individuals.
Prenatal and preimplantation genetic diagnosis are available reproductive options for families with known COL3A1 mutations.
Histological examination of affected arteries in vEDS reveals disorganized collagen fibers, fragmented elastic fibers, and increased glycosaminoglycan deposition, contributing to vessel fragility.

Classic-type EDS, caused by COL5A1 or COL5A2 mutations, is characterized by thin translucent skin, easy bruising, joint hypermobility, vascular fragility, and predisposition to aortic root dilation and dissection.
Aortic involvement in classic EDS is thought to result from defects in collagen synthesis and cross-linking, causing structural weakness and susceptibility to mechanical stress.
Next-generation sequencing identified rare, previously underexplored mutations in COL3A1 and SMAD3 in the study population, expanding the known genetic spectrum of inherited aortopathy.
The authors suggest that patients with COL3A1-associated vascular EDS may benefit from beta-blockers to reduce arterial wall stress.
Several variants of uncertain significance were identified in COL3A1 and SMAD3, with inconclusive evidence regarding their clinical relevance to aortopathy.
Gene expression of myogenic regulatory factors Pax7, Pax3, MyoD, and Myf5 showed a decreasing tendency in gastrocnemius muscle of Zip13-KO mice compared with WT mice.
The number of ITGA7-positive muscle satellite cells (MuSCs) was reduced in Zip13-KO mice compared with WT mice.
Ki67 mRNA expression was higher in Zip13-KO MuSCs than in WT MuSCs, indicating increased proliferative activity.
The proportion of quiescent-phase MuSCs (ITGA7+/CD34+) was significantly decreased while the activated-phase population (ITGA7+/CD34-) was significantly increased in Zip13-KO mice.
ZIP13 (GFP) expression and endogenous Zip13 mRNA levels were higher in quiescent-phase MuSCs than in activated-phase MuSCs in Zip13-GFP-KI mice.
Tomato-positive MuSCs (lineage-traced progeny of ZIP13-expressing cells) showed slightly increased MyoD expression, consistent with an activated-state phenotype.

After acute BaCl2-induced muscle injury, Zip13-KO mice showed delayed regeneration with persistent mononuclear cell infiltration and centrally-located nuclei at Day 10, unlike WT mice which had progressed toward peripheral nuclear migration.
During the muscle injury time course, expression of Pax7, MyoD, Atrogin, and MuRF genes was significantly reduced in Zip13-KO mice, consistent with prominent inflammation and delayed regeneration.

During muscle regeneration, GFP signal (marking quiescent MuSCs) transiently decreased at Day 20 post-injury and recovered by Day 30, while Tomato signal (marking activated/lineage progeny) remained stable, suggesting ZIP13-expressing quiescent MuSCs convert into activated MuSCs to support repair.

In Zip13-GFP-KI homozygous mice (functionally Zip13-null), GFP signal reflecting Zip13 promoter activity was significantly reduced in both quiescent and activated MuSCs compared with heterozygous mice, suggesting ZIP13 protein itself is required to sustain its own promoter activity.
During muscle regeneration, GFP expression (Zip13 promoter activity) in MuSCs of Zip13-GFP-KI homozygous mice remained low and did not recover by Day 30-40 post-injury, unlike heterozygous mice.

Loss-of-function mutations in SLC39A13/ZIP13 are established (from prior work cited by the authors) to cause Ehlers-Danlos Syndrome Spondylodysplastic Type 3 (EDSSPD3), an autosomal recessive connective tissue disorder with short stature, skeletal malformations, spinal deformities, fragile skin, and hypodontia, documented in approximately ten patients worldwide.

Prior work cited by the authors showed ZIP13 knockdown in C2C12 myoblasts impaired myogenic differentiation, and EDSSPD3 patient-derived iPSC myocytes showed impaired myogenic differentiation that was rescued by CRISPR correction of the pathological ZIP13 mutation.

The authors speculate that ZIP13 involvement in BMP/TGF-β signaling (shown previously) could form a positive feedback loop amplifying its own expression, though the precise mechanism remains to be determined.
Individuals with Hypermobility Syndrome (HMS) reported significantly higher kinesiophobia (fear of movement) scores than matched healthy controls.
Beighton hypermobility scores were significantly higher in the HMS group compared to controls, consistent with the diagnostic criteria used for group classification.
Fatigue severity, measured by the Fatigue Severity Scale, was significantly higher in HMS participants than in controls.
HMS participants reported significantly lower quality of life on the SF-36 Health Survey compared to controls.
Total objective Limits of Stability (LOS) was significantly lower in HMS individuals than in controls, reflecting impaired postural balance capacity.

LOS deficits in HMS were present across all eight tested directions (forward, backward, lateral, and diagonal), with effect sizes ranging from small to very large, the greatest deficit seen in the forward direction.
Lumbar joint repositioning errors (a measure of proprioceptive inaccuracy) in flexion, extension, and lateral bending were significantly greater in HMS participants than in controls.
Within the HMS group, lower Limits of Stability scores were moderately correlated with higher lumbar proprioception errors across flexion, extension, and lateral bending.
In a mediation model within the HMS group, higher LOS scores were associated with increased kinesiophobia levels.
In the mediation model, higher kinesiophobia was associated with worse (higher) lumbar proprioception errors, i.e., a negative path to proprioceptive accuracy.
In the mediation model, higher LOS was associated with increased fatigue severity.
In the mediation model, higher fatigue severity was associated with worse (higher) proprioception errors.
A direct path from LOS to proprioception in the mediation model showed that higher LOS was directly associated with lower (better) proprioception error.
Kinesiophobia significantly mediated the relationship between LOS and lumbar proprioception, indicating that LOS affects proprioception partly through increased fear of movement.
Fatigue significantly mediated the relationship between LOS and lumbar proprioception, indicating that LOS affects proprioception partly through increased fatigue.
The editorial notes that RCTs and systematic reviews on capsular closure during hip arthroscopy for femoroacetabular impingement syndrome show conflicting results.

The author states that closing larger incisions and T-type capsulotomy extensions is beneficial, particularly in patients at high risk of instability such as those with concomitant borderline dysplasia, hyperlaxity, or young age.

The commentary identifies concomitant hypermobility or dysplasia, along with patient age, sex, FAI type, and Tönnis grade, as intrinsic factors that may influence outcomes of hip arthroscopy independent of capsular closure.
Wandering spleen results from underdeveloped or slack splenic suspensory ligaments causing splenic hypermobility and predisposition to axial rotation/torsion.

In this patient, all six primary splenic suspensory ligaments were absent, and the spleen was suspended only by its vascular pedicle, which had undergone 270-degree clockwise torsion causing gangrenous infarction.

Contrast-enhanced abdominal CT demonstrated a classic 'whirl sign' of the twisted splenic pedicle and confirmed the ectopic location of the spleen, supporting CT as a key diagnostic modality for wandering spleen with torsion.
Because the spleen was enlarged and frankly gangrenous, splenectomy (rather than splenopexy) was performed, with a smooth postoperative recovery and discharge on day three.
Generalized joint hypermobility (GJH) has been reported as an independent risk factor for primary ACL injury.
GJH is associated with increased rotatory knee laxity in the setting of primary ACL injury.
A registry study found an inferior 2-year return to sport rate and inferior knee extension strength in patients with GJH compared with patients without GJH following primary ACL reconstruction.
One study found a compounded ACL reconstruction failure rate (graft retear, excessive graft laxity, contralateral ACL tear) of 34.1% at a mean 6-year follow-up in patients with GJH.

A recent study found a 5.53-fold increased odds of a second (ipsilateral or contralateral) ACL injury in patients with GJH compared to patients without GJH within 12 months of return to sport after primary ACL reconstruction.
The same study determined a 4.24-fold lifetime hazard ratio of second ACL injury after return to sport in patients with GJH.
Physiologic knee hyperextension is considered an independent risk factor for ACL injury, with potential contribution to inferior postoperative outcomes after ACL reconstruction.
One study found contralateral knee hyperextension of 6.5 degrees or greater was correlated with 14.6-fold odds of hamstring tendon ACL graft retear.

Hyperextension of the contralateral knee is associated with greater magnitudes of anterior tibial translation of the ACL-injured knee after ACL reconstruction, and knee hyperextension was determined to be a risk factor for postoperative ACL graft laxity.

Several recent studies did not find a clinically meaningful relationship between the magnitude of knee hyperextension and postoperative knee laxity, subjective knee function, or revision surgery risk.
The presence of knee hyperextensibility was reported to increase the predictive potential of the Beighton score for residual high-grade pivot shift after ACL reconstruction.
Knee hyperextension of 5 degrees or more was reported to be present in one third of patients undergoing revision ACL reconstruction.
Serum DOT1L (disruptor of telomeric silencing 1-like) levels were significantly higher in fibromyalgia patients than in healthy controls.
Serum DOT1L levels positively correlated with Fibromyalgia Impact Questionnaire (FIQ) scores in FM patients.
Serum DOT1L levels positively correlated with pain intensity as measured by the Visual Analog Scale (VAS) in FM patients.
Serum DOT1L levels positively correlated with the Widespread Pain Index (WPI) in FM patients.
Serum DOT1L levels positively correlated with the Symptom Severity Score (SSS) in FM patients.
Serum DOT1L levels positively correlated with sleep quality impairment as measured by the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI) in FM patients.
Serum DOT1L levels positively correlated with fatigue severity (FSS) in FM patients.
Serum DOT1L levels positively correlated with anxiety symptoms (Hospital Anxiety Scale) in FM patients.
Serum DOT1L levels positively correlated with depressive symptoms (Hospital Depression Scale) in FM patients.
DOT1L was a statistically significant predictor of FM status in logistic regression, and ROC analysis identified a cutoff of 0.315 ng/mL with 79% sensitivity and 71.7% specificity for detecting FM.
Serum triglyceride levels were significantly higher in FM patients compared to healthy controls.
Total cholesterol levels were significantly higher in FM patients compared to healthy controls.
LDL cholesterol levels were significantly higher in FM patients compared to healthy controls.

No significant differences were found between FM patients and controls for glucose, urea, creatinine, uric acid, albumin, HDL cholesterol, total bilirubin, ALT, AST, CRP, hemoglobin, lymphocyte, neutrophil, TSH, free T3, or free T4 levels.
Fecal calprotectin levels were significantly higher in fibromyalgia patients with gastrointestinal symptoms compared to healthy controls.
Fecal calprotectin levels did not differ significantly between FMS patients without GI symptoms and FMS patients with GI symptoms.
Fecal calprotectin levels did not differ significantly between FMS patients without GI symptoms and healthy controls.
The number of fecal calprotectin-positive subjects (>50 μg/g) was similar across the three groups.
Fibromyalgia symptom duration was significantly longer in patients with gastrointestinal symptoms than in those without.
Widespread pain index scores were significantly higher in FMS patients with gastrointestinal symptoms than in those without.
Symptom severity scale scores were significantly higher in FMS patients with gastrointestinal symptoms than in those without.
A weak positive correlation was found between fibromyalgia disease duration and symptom severity scale scores.
No correlation was found between fecal calprotectin levels and any clinical parameters assessed.
A cited study found that 72.5% of chronic pain patients had comorbid ADHD.
ADHD medications reduced pain NRS scores by 3.5 points, a 61.5% improvement, in chronic pain patients with comorbid ADHD.
ADHD frequently coexists with nociplastic pain conditions including fibromyalgia, chronic low back pain, idiopathic orofacial pain, chronic chest pain, and chronic abdominal pain.

ADHD medications given to patients with nociplastic pain have been shown to regulate blood flow in pain-matrix brain regions including the prefrontal cortex, precuneus, anterior cingulate cortex, and insular cortex.
Increased precuneus blood flow correlated positively with nociplastic pain severity, and methylphenidate responders showed significantly higher precuneus blood flow before treatment than after.
Methylphenidate alleviated motor control problems and elevated muscle tension in individuals with ADHD.
ADHD medications improved family relationships, a psychosocial factor that contributes to the maintenance and worsening of chronic pain.
Spontaneously hypertensive rats (SHR), a rodent ADHD model, showed weaker noxious stimulus-induced analgesia compared to control rats.
In SHR, stimulus-evoked norepinephrine concentration in the spinal dorsal horn decreased compared to controls, suggesting weakened endogenous descending analgesia in the ADHD model.

In spinal cord slices, SHR showed a larger immunostained area for norepinephrine-synthesizing enzymes and higher extracellular norepinephrine levels in the dorsal horn under pain-free conditions than controls.

SHR showed larger norepinephrine transporter (NET) staining but smaller α2A receptor staining than controls, indicating NET overexpression and α2A receptor downregulation associated with reduced descending pain inhibition.
6-OHDA ADHD model mice displayed shorter latency and lower threshold to thermal/mechanical nociceptive stimuli than controls, indicating heightened baseline nociceptive sensitivity.
In 6-OHDA mice, excitatory synaptic connections in spinal dorsal horn lamina II were significantly increased compared to controls, while inhibitory connections were unchanged.
In 6-OHDA-induced ADHD mice, spontaneous activity in the anterior cingulate cortex-posterior insula (ACC-PI) pathway was higher, and mechanically-evoked ACC activity was stronger, than in controls.
Inhibiting the ACC-PI pathway in 6-OHDA mice suppressed dorsal horn action potential firing and raised the pain threshold, indicating a causal role of ACC-PI hyperactivity in central sensitization.

A sex-specific neuroinflammatory response to dopamine neuron depletion was reported in 6-OHDA mice: males showed ACC-restricted inflammation causing hyperactivity without hyperalgesia, while females showed ACC-PI pathway inflammation causing hyperalgesia without hyperactivity, and reducing this inflammation alleviated hyperalgesia.
Atomoxetine, a selective norepinephrine reuptake inhibitor used for ADHD, improved both hyperalgesia from central sensitization and ADHD symptoms (hyperactivity, inattention) in SHR and 6-OHDA mice.
More than 33% of children and over 50% of adults discontinue FDA-approved ADHD medications within a year due to suboptimal efficacy or tolerance issues.
Pramipexole, a dopamine agonist used in Parkinson's disease and effective for ADHD, has been reported to improve chronic low back pain and fibromyalgia.
Risperidone's effectiveness for treating ADHD symptoms has been reported to be comparable to that of methylphenidate.
Lithium's effectiveness in treating ADHD has been reported to be comparable to that of methylphenidate.
Clonidine, an α2 agonist and antihypertensive, is considered effective for treating both ADHD and chronic pain.
Hyperactivity caused by high extracellular dopamine levels in 6-OHDA mice was regulated and improved by enhancing serotonergic tone.
Spinal cord PEA concentrations were significantly lower in HbSS sickle cell mice than in sex-matched HbAA control mice, in both males and females.
OEA was significantly reduced only in female HbSS mice compared with female HbAA controls, with no change observed in males.
No difference was found in spinal cord AEA or DHEA concentrations between HbSS and HbAA mice.
2-LG was significantly reduced in male HbSS mice compared with male HbAA mice and was undetectable in female mice of either genotype.
Systemic administration of the NAAA inhibitor ARN dose-dependently reduced mechanical and cold hyperalgesia in male HbSS mice over 72 hours.
PEA dose-dependently reduced mechanical and cold hyperalgesia in male HbSS mice, with no effect in male or female control HbAA mice.
Female HbSS mice showed constitutively greater cold hyperalgesia at baseline than male HbSS mice.

In female HbSS mice, PEA at 20 mg/kg/day reduced mechanical and cold hyperalgesia to a similar extent as in males, and additionally showed modest improvement in spontaneous musculoskeletal hyperalgesia and reduced cold aversion in a nonevoked test.
PEA reduced hyperalgesia to a similar extent as the mixed CB1R/CB2R agonist CP55,940 in female HbSS mice, suggesting comparable efficacy without cannabinoid intoxication.
Spinal cord MDA, a marker of lipid peroxidation/oxidative stress, was elevated in female HbSS mice compared with female HbAA mice, and PEA treatment significantly reduced it.
Spinal cord IL-1β and caspase-3 activity were increased in female HbSS mice compared with HbAA mice, and 14-day PEA treatment significantly reduced both.
ROCK activity was significantly elevated in HbSS spinal cords compared with HbAA mice, and this was abrogated by 14-day PEA treatment.
A sickle microenvironment induced with TNF-α and hemin significantly increased ROCK activity in differentiated PC12 cells, which was ameliorated by NEP1-40 or PEA treatment.
PEA treatment (20 mg/kg/day) significantly reduced spinal cord p38-MAPK phosphorylation in vivo, a pathway involved in chronic pain sensitization.
TNF-α/hemin exposure substantially increased phospho-p38-MAPK levels and nuclear translocation in primary DRG neurons from HbSS mice, and this was almost completely abrogated by PEA cotreatment.

Oral neflamapimod dose-dependently improved mechanical and cold hyperalgesia and cold tolerance over 14 days in female HbSS mice, without affecting musculoskeletal hyperalgesia (grip force), confirming a role for p38-MAPK in chronic hyperalgesia.
Skin biopsies showed significantly increased mast cell degranulation in female HbSS mice compared with female HbAA mice, which was significantly reduced by 14-day PEA treatment.
Skin releasate tryptase, a mast cell activation marker, was significantly higher in HbSS mice than HbAA mice and was significantly reduced by PEA treatment.
HbSS mice had constitutively elevated IL-6 in skin releasate and circulating SAP compared with HbAA mice, both of which were significantly reduced by 14-day PEA treatment.

A cytokine microarray of skin releasate showed that PEA treatment significantly reduced multiple mast cell-associated and pro-inflammatory cytokines (IL-1β, IL-5, IL-6, IL-17, IFN-γ, TNF-α, IL-10, IL-12) in HbSS mice compared with vehicle.

In primary mast cells from HbSS mouse skin, a sickle microenvironment (TNF-α + hemin) induced MCET formation, which was dose-dependently attenuated by PEA, similarly to the CB1R/CB2R agonist CP55,940.

Hypoxia/reoxygenation exacerbated mechanical and cold hyperalgesia in female HbSS mice, modeling acute vaso-occlusive crisis pain, and PEA pretreatment blocked this H/R-evoked hyperalgesia throughout a 14-day treatment period.

A single dose of PEA given immediately after a first H/R incitement significantly reduced acute mechanical and cold hyperalgesia, but this effect did not persist after a second H/R incitement without further treatment.

A single dose of PEA maintained improved grip force (less musculoskeletal hyperalgesia) after a second H/R incitement compared with vehicle, suggesting a persistent disease-modifying effect on nonevoked pain.

CD300lf and CD300a colocalize with phosphatidylserine externalized to the outer leaflet of the plasma membrane in a polar formation upon mast cell activation, and CD300lf cooperates with CD300a to inhibit BMMC activation.

CD300lf also colocalizes with extracellular ceramide in addition to internal phosphatidylserine on the mast cell surface, producing stronger inhibition of mast cell activation than binding to phosphatidylserine alone.

Both Cd300a-/- and Cd300lf-/- mice showed greater drops in rectal temperature than wild-type mice in a passive systemic anaphylaxis model, indicating loss of either inhibitory receptor worsens mast cell-driven anaphylaxis.

Double knockout Cd300a-/-Cd300lf-/- mice exhibited an even lower rectal temperature than either single knockout during passive systemic anaphylaxis, demonstrating that CD300a and CD300lf cooperatively limit mast cell activation in vivo.
Tocilizumab (IL-6 receptor blockade) induced complete clinical remission of systemic juvenile idiopathic arthritis by the sixth monthly infusion.

During tocilizumab treatment for JIA, the patient's IgE-mediated food allergies to cow's milk, egg, and peanut resolved, with negative skin prick tests, normalized specific IgE, and tolerance on oral food challenge.

IL-6 is proposed to have a dual pathogenic role, driving Th17-mediated autoinflammation in systemic JIA while also promoting Th2 differentiation, IgE class switching, and mast cell activation relevant to food allergy.

A prior study found that a single dose of tocilizumab did not significantly prevent allergen-induced bronchoconstriction in patients with mild allergic asthma, contrasting with the allergy resolution observed in this case.
The patient's total serum IgE level at initial presentation was markedly elevated relative to the reference range, consistent with atopic/IgE-mediated food allergy.
Peanut-specific IgE remained persistently high at two time points prior to allergy resolution, supporting classification of the peanut allergy as persistent rather than naturally transient.

Comprehensive immunological workup (lymphocyte subsets, immunoglobulins, complement levels) was normal, and the patient lacked features of DOCK8 deficiency, ruling out a known inborn error of immunity as the cause of concurrent JIA and severe food allergy.

Molecular docking and post-docking simulations of diverse MRGPRX2 ligands identified a common pharmacophore requiring at least one protonated amine moiety forming a salt-bridge and π-cation interaction, plus an extended non-polar surface domain enabling hydrophobic and/or π-stacking interactions.

Seven specific MRGPRX2 receptor residues (GLU164, ASP184, PHE101, PHE170, TRP243, PHE244, PHE257) were identified as key interaction sites mediating hydrogen bonding, salt-bridges, π-cation interactions and π-π stacking that direct ligand binding and receptor activation.
Maternal α-tocopherol supplementation blocked development of peanut extract (PNE)-specific IgE sensitization in pups co-exposed to Alternaria alternata and PNE.

α-tocopherol supplementation did not reduce Alt+PNE-stimulated increases in skin IL33, amphiregulin (Areg), oncostatin M (OSM), CCL11, TSLP, or plasma mast cell protease MCPT1, indicating these upstream alarmin/cytokine responses were unaffected by treatment.
Maternal α-tocopherol supplementation blocked mast cell activation in Alt+PNE sensitized pups.
α-tocopherol supplementation prevented the rise in plasma histamine that otherwise occurs in Alt+PNE sensitized pups.
Maternal α-tocopherol supplementation blocked histamine receptor (H1R)-mediated stimulation of endothelial PKCα signaling that otherwise occurred following Alt+PNE sensitization.
Sarcoidosis patients without SFN were significantly more likely to be male than sarcoidosis patients with probable SFN.
Sarcoidosis patients, both with and without SFN, had significantly higher BMI than healthy controls.
Fatigue prevalence was higher in sarcoidosis patients with SFN (96%) than in those without SFN (84%).
Extreme fatigue (FAS>34) was more prevalent in sarcoidosis patients with SFN (60%) than without SFN (39%).
Mean pain over the past 7 days was reported far more frequently in sarcoidosis patients with SFN (85%) than without SFN (33%).
Maximum pain over the past 7 days was reported far more frequently in sarcoidosis patients with SFN (92%) than without SFN (45%).
RLS prevalence was higher in sarcoidosis patients with SFN (67%) than without SFN (41%).
Cognitive impairment prevalence did not differ significantly between sarcoidosis patients with SFN (46%) and without SFN (35%).
Sarcoidosis patients overall scored higher on fatigue, mean pain, maximum pain, RLS, and cognitive failure questionnaires than healthy controls.
Within sarcoidosis patients, those with SFN showed greater severity of fatigue, mean pain, maximum pain, and RLS than those without SFN.
Although prevalence of cognitive impairment did not differ significantly, its severity measured by CFQ was significantly higher in sarcoidosis patients with SFN than without SFN.

In sarcoidosis patients with SFN, fatigue, mean pain, maximum pain, RLS, and cognitive failure scores were all significantly correlated with each other, with FAS showing correlations above 0.5 with all other measures.
Despite the overall sarcoidosis cohort being male-dominated (58%), the SFN subgroup showed female predominance (56%) while the non-SFN subgroup showed male predominance (73%).
Among healthy controls, 15% had an elevated FAS score indicating fatigue, consistent with prior general population data showing about 20% of healthy individuals score above the fatigue cutoff.
Small RCTs cited in the discussion suggest that neurostimulants (methylphenidate, armodafinil) or steroids (dexamethasone) could improve sarcoidosis-associated fatigue.
A cited study reported improvements in fatigue in sarcoidosis patients after a 12-week online mindfulness-based cognitive therapy.
Lower serum magnesium levels were strongly associated with reduced corneal nerve fiber length (CNFL), a marker of small fiber neuropathy, in patients with type 2 diabetes.
Lower serum magnesium levels were moderately associated with reduced corneal nerve fiber density (CNFD) in patients with type 2 diabetes.
Lower serum magnesium levels were moderately associated with reduced corneal nerve branch density (CNBD) in patients with type 2 diabetes.

After adjusting for age, sex, diabetes duration, BMI, blood pressure, HbA1c, FBG, triglyceride, TC, eGFR, and fasting C-peptide, serum magnesium remained independently and positively associated with CNFL, CNFD, and CNBD.

Fasting blood glucose (FBG) was negatively correlated with all three corneal nerve morphological parameters (CNFL, CNFD, CNBD), consistent with higher glucose being associated with worse small fiber neuropathy.
Fasting C-peptide levels were positively correlated with CNFL, CNFD, and CNBD, suggesting a protective association against corneal small fiber neuropathy.
HbA1c was inversely correlated with corneal nerve fiber length (CNFL), consistent with higher long-term glycemia being associated with worse small fiber neuropathy.
Longer duration of diabetes was negatively correlated with corneal nerve fiber density (CNFD), indicating worsening small fiber neuropathy with disease chronicity.
BMI was positively correlated with CNFD and CNBD, an unexpected direction given BMI's usual role as a diabetes risk factor.
HDL cholesterol was inversely correlated with CNFL and CNBD, an unexpected direction given HDL's usual protective role in diabetes.
Patients in lower serum magnesium quartiles had progressively lower corneal nerve fiber length, density, and branch density compared to higher quartiles.

Decreased serum magnesium is proposed to exacerbate oxidative stress and inflammation by attenuating oxidative stress kinases and upregulating pro-inflammatory factors such as TNF-α, IL-6, and IL-8, which may underlie corneal small fiber neuropathy pathogenesis.
Colonic EV miR-23a and miR-23b levels were significantly lower in patients with PI-IBS-D than in controls, confirmed by both microarray and TaqMan PCR.
Colon biopsy tissue from PI-IBS-D patients also showed decreased miR-23a/b expression, with colocalization confirmed by FISH.
miR-155 was significantly increased in colonic EVs and colon biopsies of PI-IBS-D patients and was used as a positive control marker.
Colonic EV and colon tissue miR-23a/b expression was inversely correlated with VAS abdominal pain scores in PI-IBS-D patients.
miR-23a/b expression did not differ significantly among PI-IBS-D subgroups defined by prior infectious agent (Campylobacter, Salmonella, Shiga toxin-producing E. coli).
A highly conserved miR-23a/b binding site with perfect seed complementarity was identified in the 3'-UTR of Grin2B mRNA, and luciferase reporter assays confirmed miR-23a/b directly targets Grin2B.
NMDA NR2B protein expression was reduced in human neurons following transfection with lenti-miR-23a/b precursor compared with lenti-control precursor.
NMDA NR2B expression was higher in colonic EVs from PI-IBS-D patients than in control participants, as shown by real-time PCR.
NMDA NR2B protein levels were significantly increased in colon biopsy tissue of PI-IBS-D patients versus controls by ELISA and immunohistochemistry.
NMDA NR2B expression in colonic EVs and colon tissue positively correlated with VAS abdominal pain scores in PI-IBS-D patients.
Laser capture microdissection showed NR2B, but not NR2A, NR2C, or NR2D, was selectively upregulated in colonic neurons of PI-IBS-D patients, colocalizing with the neuronal marker anti-Hu.
No significant differences in any NMDA NR2 subtype (NR2A-D) expression were observed in colonic epithelial cells between PI-IBS-D patients and controls, indicating the effect is neuron-specific.
CXCR4 and CXCL12, additional predicted targets of miR-23a/b, were upregulated in both colonic neuronal cells and epithelial cells of PI-IBS-D patients compared with controls.
NR2B expression in colon biopsies did not differ significantly among PI-IBS-D subgroups by preceding infectious pathogen.

Coincubating human neuronal cells with PI-IBS-D colonic EVs progressively increased NMDA NR2B expression (significant by 48 hours) while decreasing miR-23a and miR-23b expression at 24, 48, and 72 hours.

Coincubation of mouse dorsal root ganglia with PI-IBS-D colonic EVs increased NMDA NR2B expression at 48-72 hours and decreased miR-23a (from 24h) and miR-23b (from 48h) expression, with endocytosis of EVs confirmed by confocal microscopy.
Human colonoids incubated with PI-IBS-D colonic EVs for 48 hours showed significantly increased GAS5 and decreased miR-23a/b expression, with EV endocytosis into colonoids confirmed microscopically.

Intraperitoneal injection of PI-IBS-D colonic EVs into mice induced visceral hypersensitivity, with a ~50% increase in visceromotor response to colorectal distension compared with mice given control EVs, emerging at day 5 and reaching significance at day 7.

P-EV mice (injected with PI-IBS-D colonic EVs) showed increased NMDA NR2B expression in colon and DRG tissue and decreased DRG miR-23a/b expression relative to baseline, changes not observed in C-EV mice.
Laser capture microdissection showed that among NMDA receptor subunits, only NR2B (not NR2A, NR2C, or NR2D) was significantly upregulated in colonic neurons of PI-IBS-D patients.

No significant differences were observed in NMDA NR2A, NR2B, NR2C, or NR2D expression in colonic epithelial cells between PI-IBS-D patients and controls, indicating neuron-specific NR2B dysregulation.
CXCR4, an additional miR-23a/b target, was upregulated in both colonic neuronal cells and colonic epithelial cells of PI-IBS-D patients compared with controls.
CXCL12, another miR-23a/b target, was similarly upregulated in colonic neuronal and epithelial cells of PI-IBS-D patients compared with controls.
NR2B expression in human colon biopsies did not differ significantly among PI-IBS-D subgroups defined by prior Campylobacter, Salmonella, or Shiga toxin-producing E. coli infection.
Coincubation of human neuronal cells with PI-IBS-D colonic EVs increased NMDA NR2B expression by 24-48 hours while decreasing miR-23a and miR-23b expression from 24 through 72 hours.
Coincubation of mouse dorsal root ganglia (DRGs) with PI-IBS-D colonic EVs increased NMDA NR2B expression at 48-72 hours while decreasing miR-23a and miR-23b expression starting at 24-48 hours.
Confocal microscopy demonstrated endocytosis of human colonic EVs into neuronal cells in culture within 8 hours of coincubation, supporting direct EV-neuron communication.
In human colonoids incubated with PI-IBS-D colonic EVs, GAS5 expression significantly increased by 48 hours while miR-23a and miR-23b decreased.

Intraperitoneal injection of colonic EVs from PI-IBS-D patients into mice (P-EV mice) caused a ~50% increase in visceromotor response (VMR) to colorectal distension compared with mice injected with control EVs, significant from day 7 and persisting to day 12.
Colonic NMDA NR2B expression was upregulated relative to baseline in P-EV mice from day 7 through day 12, an effect not observed in C-EV mice.
DRG NMDA NR2B expression increased in P-EV mice at days 7, 10, and 12 post colonic EV injection, but not in C-EV mice.
DRG miR-23a expression decreased relative to baseline at days 5, 7, 10 and 12 in P-EV mice, while DRG miR-23b decreased at days 7, 10, and 12.

Rab27a/b-/- mice, which are deficient in EV secretion, showed only a slight, nonsignificant increase in visceral nociception after injection with PI-IBS-D colonic EVs, indicating EVs are required internal messengers for the effect.

In the mouse EV-injection model, miR-23a/b and NR2B expression did not differ significantly between subgroups of PI-IBS-D patients grouped by prior Campylobacter, Salmonella, or Shiga toxin-producing E. coli infection.

Intraperitoneal treatment with a lenti-miR-23a/b mimic significantly reduced VMR to colorectal distension in P-EV mice compared with lenti-miR-scramble control, and significantly enhanced DRG miR-23a expression.
Injection of naked miR-23 oligonucleotides without an EV or lentiviral carrier failed to significantly reduce VMR to colorectal distension or change DRG miR-23a expression in P-EV mice.

Mechanically inserting a miR-23 oligonucleotide mimic into purified human EVs and injecting them into P-EV mice produced a large reduction in VMR to colorectal distension at days 5 and 7, and enhanced DRG miR-23a expression, compared with EV-carried scrambled miR control.

Intraperitoneal injection of colonic EVs from PI-IBS-D patients into mice increased the visceromotor response to colorectal distension by about 50% compared with mice given control EVs, becoming statistically significant by day 7 and persisting to day 12.
Colonic NMDA NR2B expression increased above baseline in P-EV mice starting day 7 and continuing through day 12, an effect not seen in C-EV mice.
DRG NMDA NR2B expression increased in P-EV mice at days 7, 10, and 12 after colonic EV injection, an effect not observed in C-EV mice.
DRG miR-23a expression decreased relative to baseline at days 5, 7, 10, and 12 in P-EV mice.
DRG miR-23b expression decreased at days 7, 10, and 12 in P-EV mice relative to baseline.

No significant differences in miR-23a/b and NR2B expression were found among mouse groups injected with EVs from patients with different antecedent enteric infections (Campylobacter, Salmonella, Shiga toxin-producing E. coli).

Rab27a/b-/- mice, which are deficient in EV secretion, showed no significant increase in visceral nociception (VMR to CD) after injection with colonic EVs from PI-IBS-D patients, indicating EVs are essential internal messengers for the effect.
In P-EV mice, i.p. injection of lenti-miR-23 mimic significantly decreased the VMR to colorectal distension compared with lenti-miR-scramble control.
Injection of miR-23 oligonucleotide alone, without an EV or lentiviral carrier, did not significantly reduce the VMR to colorectal distension in P-EV mice.

Mechanically loading miR-23 oligonucleotide into purified human colonic EVs and injecting these into P-EV mice produced a large, significant reduction in visceral hypersensitivity at days 5 and 7 compared with EV-carried scrambled control.
DRG miR-23a expression was significantly enhanced in P-EV mice after i.p. injection of lenti-miR-23, but unchanged after injection of free miR-23 oligonucleotide without a carrier.

FISH/IHC double labeling of mouse DRGs showed that EV-carried oligo-miR-23a mimic treatment increased miR-23a and decreased NMDA NR2B expression, with colocalization of the two, whereas EV-carried scrambled control increased NR2B and decreased miR-23a.
FISH analysis showed increased miR-23a expression in mouse colon tissue after 7 days of treatment with EV-carried oligo-miR-23a mimic, unlike mice given scrambled control.
Using the Human Inflammatory Response and Autoimmunity lncRNA PCR array, GAS5 and SNHG20 expression levels were significantly increased in colonic EVs from PI-IBS-D patients compared with controls.
Bioinformatic prediction (RegRNA 2.0) identified four lncRNAs — NEAT1, MALAT1, GAS5, and MEG3 — with sequences complementary to miR-23, but not SNHG20.
lncRNA GAS5 expression was significantly upregulated in colon tissue of PI-IBS-D patients compared with control participants.
lncRNA GAS5 expression was significantly upregulated in colonic EVs of PI-IBS-D patients compared with control participants.
GAS5 was the only lncRNA of those tested that was significantly upregulated in DRGs of P-EV mice compared with C-EV mice.

Dual-luciferase assays confirmed direct binding between lncRNA GAS5 and miR-23a/b: luciferase activity of psiCHECK-2-GAS5-wt was reduced after cotransfection with miR-23a/b mimic, while activity of the negative control and the GAS5 mutant construct remained unchanged.
RNA pull-down assays showed that miR-23a pulled down 74% of total GAS5 in human colon tissue and 62% of GAS5 in mouse DRGs, confirming direct binding.
Silencing lncRNA GAS5 in human neuronal cells (LUHMES) via lentiviral transduction increased miR-23a expression, indicating GAS5 directly binds and sequesters miR-23a.
Silencing lncRNA GAS5 in human neuronal cells significantly downregulated NMDA NR2B expression.
GAS5 colocalized with a neuronal marker and with NMDA NR2B in colon tissue from PI-IBS-D patients, supporting a neuronal site of the GAS5-NR2B interaction.
In vivo knockdown of GAS5 using Vivo-Morpholino administered to P-EV mice on day 5 significantly decreased the VMR to colorectal distension two days later compared with controls.
GAS5-Vivo-Morpholino treatment in P-EV mice increased miR-23a/b expression and decreased NMDA NR2B expression in mouse DRGs two days after treatment.
Single-cell PCR in colonic neuronal cells showed significantly increased miR-23a/b expression and decreased NMDA NR2B expression after i.p. injection of GAS5-Vivo-Morpholino.

In colonic epithelial cells, GAS5-Vivo-Morpholino significantly increased miR-23a/b expression, but NMDA NR2B expression remained unchanged, indicating the GAS5-miR-23-NR2B effect is neuron-specific rather than epithelial.
PPI network analysis identified nine hub genes (SPP1, POSTN, CCN2, FGF7, OGN, BMP2, LUM, TGFB2, BMP7) as candidate diagnostic biomarkers for ischemic heart failure.
FGF7 expression was reduced in rat models of left anterior descending coronary artery ligation.
BMP7 expression was reduced in rat models of left anterior descending coronary artery ligation.
TGFB2 expression was elevated in rat models of left anterior descending coronary artery ligation.
OGN expression was elevated in rat models of left anterior descending coronary artery ligation.
CCN2 expression was elevated in rat models of left anterior descending coronary artery ligation.
Knockdown of TGFB2 promoted cell viability and inhibited apoptosis in oxygen-glucose deprivation-induced H9c2 cardiomyocytes.
Knockdown of TGFB2 increased cell viability and decreased apoptosis in oxygen-glucose deprivation-induced H9c2 cardiomyoblasts.
TGFB2 knockdown decreased the ratio of cleaved Caspase-3 to total Caspase-3 protein levels in OGD-induced H9c2 cells.
TGFB2 knockdown decreased Bax protein levels in OGD-induced H9c2 cells.
TGFB2 knockdown increased Bcl-2 protein expression in OGD-induced H9c2 cells.
Escin treatment markedly reduced dorsal skin and ear lesion severity in DFE-induced AD mice, and this benefit was abolished by co-treatment with the GR antagonist RU486.
Escin treatment markedly decreased the clinical dermatitis severity score compared to DFE-treated mice, and RU486 pre-treatment significantly increased the score relative to escin treatment.
Escin-treated mice had lower ear thickness than DFE-treated mice, an effect blocked by RU486 pre-treatment.
DFE-induced inflammation caused spleen and lymph node enlargement, which was mitigated by escin, an effect blocked by RU486 pre-treatment.
Epidermal thickness was significantly greater in DFE-treated mice than controls, and escin treatment reduced this DFE-induced epidermal thickening.
Escin treatment significantly decreased dermal mast cell infiltration (toluidine blue staining) compared to DFE-treated mice, and this reduction was reversed by RU486 pre-treatment.
Serum IgE levels were elevated 15-fold in DFE-treated mice relative to controls, and this increase was inhibited by escin but restored by RU486 pre-treatment.
TSLP expression was elevated in DFE-treated skin by IHC, and escin inhibited this DFE-induced increase, an effect attenuated by RU486.
DFE reduced filaggrin expression in the epidermis compared to controls, and escin treatment restored filaggrin levels, an effect blocked by RU486.
GR protein levels significantly increased in dorsal skin of escin-treated mice compared to control and DFE groups, and this increase was reversed by RU486.
Elevated NF-κB levels in DFE-treated skin were reduced by escin, but RU486 pre-treatment restored NF-κB expression to levels comparable with the DFE group.
Serum/skin TSLP levels decreased from 223.49 ± 17.95 pg/ml in DFE-treated mice to 107.62 ± 25.54 pg/ml with escin treatment, an effect reversed by RU486 pre-treatment.
Escin decreased skin levels of IL-4, IL-13, TNF-α, and IL-1β compared to DFE-treated mice, and these reductions were notably reversed by RU486 pre-treatment.
Escin promoted HaCaT keratinocyte proliferation at 0.3-3 μg/ml but was cytotoxic at 10 μg/ml.
In unstimulated HaCaT cells, escin reduced TSLP expression while increasing filaggrin expression.
TNF-α/IFN-γ stimulation increased TSLP and decreased filaggrin expression in HaCaT cells, effects reversed by escin, and RU486 pre-treatment prevented escin's effect.
NF-κB expression changes induced by escin in TNF-α/IFN-γ-stimulated HaCaT cells were reversed by RU486.
Escin showed cytotoxicity in RAW 264.7 macrophages at concentrations of 4 μg/ml and higher, so 1 and 3 μg/ml were selected for further study.
Escin effectively suppressed LPS-induced nitric oxide secretion in RAW 264.7 macrophages.
Escin inhibited the LPS-induced increase in iNOS and COX-2 expression in RAW 264.7 macrophages.
Escin significantly suppressed LPS-induced IL-1β and IL-6 expression in RAW 264.7 macrophages.
